notes.title: Bug fixes & big update to prepare for Online cross-play
notes.notes:
A lot of core update had to be done to prepare for the Online cross-play with console.

Including some core libraries and engine updates, we've done our best to avoid any bugs but there might be still a few sneaky ones that made their way in as there are a log of big changes.

Please be patient and do let us know on Steam of Discord if you run into any bugs!

We also fixes the old ones we were aware of:

Changelog:
+ Major updates to prepare for cross-play.
+ Fix broken achievements "Skynet Wins".
+ Improve Chinese translations.
+ Fix game stuck in local when last two players are punched at the same time.
+ Fix lighting issues on mac and linux.
+ Fix bot speed being different at lower fps.

notes.title: You can now play from 2 to 8 players
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36777231/428e335cf471260412394dbeffb1a60f57917b1a.png[/img]

As you can imagine, it can get a bit crazy on some levels with 8 players, but you can come up with a lot of new strategies to punch all of your friends!

[h2][New feature] Round timers:[/h2]
The default way to play is still with unlimited time to blend in the crowds of AIs for as long as you want, but we added an option to limit the rounds in time.

With 8 players, if there are experiences differences between players, it can get a bit long for the one who always dies early, so you can now set a limit of 1 to 4 minutes per round!

At the end of the timer, all remaining players are revealed and the level ends. 
Make sure you're ready to throw a few punches in the last few seconds!

[h2]New avatars[/h2]
We added 5 new unlockable avatars, here is a sneak peak at one of them:
https://youtube.com/shorts/DijRIUiUAds

Now that's out, we'll be focusing fully on the new levels and the online mode! :)

The GrosChevaux team

We have been busy, turns out releasing a first game is a lot of work!  :D

Sorry, no new levels or online mode quite yet but a small update to fix some annoying bugs.

We are currently focusing on getting the console versions ready (we're getting there, we'll give you updates as soon as we have anything concrete).

The demo also got an update as it was a bit old, you can now play meadow, Sushi Bar and Prison for free.


Here is the changelog:

[b]Features & Gameplay:
[/b]- Battlefield: First bombs are slower to give players more time to find their character.
- Disco: Level brighter to avoid losing characters in the dark.
- Supero: New character designs.

[b]Bug Fixes:[/b]
- Spaceship: Stop ability to use both distracts at once.
- Supero: Add missing sounds when player collect all items.
- Fix wrong titles in end screen.
- Menus and end title screen control improvements.
- On start screen, pressing 'shift' doesn't not create a new player to avoid clashing with Steam overlay shortcut .
- Tried optimizatiosn for Parsec sound issue. (Should be fixed but please let us know if you have sound issues on Parsec!).
- Various fixes.

[b]Performance Improvements:
[/b]- Fix Medium performance mode.
- Improve lights in Fast mode, to improve performance on older machines.

notes.title: Unspottable is Out!
notes.notes:
We are so excited to release our first game today!
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36777231/f167d0e592634b2d7410d0058405926fa473837b.gif[/img]

First, we have a very cool launch trailer for you all:
[previewyoutube=_3WolAhKFnw;full][/previewyoutube]


Unspottable is a competitive party game for 2 to 4 players that will test you on whether you can tell your friends from machines.

Hide amongst a crowd of AIs in 12 different environments with specific gameplay mechanics:
+ Revealing spotlights
+ Falling Bombs+ Punching Robots
+ Sidequests and more...

And an expert mode for experienced players who want to push the deception and mind games.

"Walk like a robot, Punch like a Human!"

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36777231/7d7792aaebb5388a77dedb957762ac3808706240.gif[/img]


The game is local multiplayer only, no singleplayer, no in-game online mode.You can play online though, using services like Steam remote play. 
It has been live saver for us during this weird year where we have to do all our testing remotely!!

Thank you to everyone who gave us feedback on the demo during all the online events we attended this year, we hope you'll enjoy the game as much as we've enjoyed making it! :)

Consoles builds are almost there, so we should be able to release on Switch, Xbox One and PS4 in November!

We love to hear what you think, come chat on [url=https://twitter.com/UnspottableGame]twitter [/url] and [url=https://t.co/D9odSIV9nz?amp=1]discord[/url]!

notes.title: New Level Alert! Presenting the Spaceship!
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36777231/6a10e9e459cfe4576f9d475cde57264bf26e90da.png[/img]

As the release is approaching, (we're going to announce a date for the PC, mac and Linux release very soon) we can now show more of the last few levels!

[b]Presenting the spaceship![/b]

In the game we want to introduce a new mechanic per level.
One of the mechanic we wanted to play with from the start was the teleportation, it seemed to be a pretty obvious one to work with the concept of the game, so we started with this idea:

[i]"A players enters a teleporter, they come out another one and two robots come out of other teleporters."[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36777231/f06cabb980db63b4934caed5627c7f45607ac520.gif[/img]


Testing this mechanic was fun but still missing something, teleporting is useful if you've been seen but it's also risky, the other players will know you are one of the three characters that just appeared.

So it was still missing a reason to force or encourage the players to teleport!

We had been toying with the idea of getting the player in a position where they get in trouble randomly but have a way to escape, to add a bit of tension, unpredictability and so players have a rush of adrenaline when they are at the wrong place, at the wrong time.

For that we made the 'electrocution areas'. (We don't have a name for that, we call them electric pizza slices between us!).
[i]When the zone get electrified, the teleporter activates, and all the robots in the area die and disappear, leaving the player standing there on their own, visible to everyone! :)[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36777231/5e77a1d00eb983fbbffb48e68064365c426f1aae.gif[/img]


This worked very well in test sessions, we just wanted the level to be a bit more intense, so we added the ability for player to teleport twice as they want using the distract button, that can lead to some good chain teleporting where keeping track of everyone becomes very challenging and lead to some fun situations! :D

This required a good readbility, so we worked on good FX to show what is happening. :)

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36777231/6d8bb11c53cb509559bae00bb80886ee88b15414.gif[/img]

If you are not too familiar with the game, you can check out the trailer here:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7OnYZgg-qlo&ab_channel=GrosChevaux

We can't wait for you all to play this level!!

If you want to help us, play the demo with your friends and [b]wishlist [/b]the game!

Join us on twitter or [url=https://t.co/D9odSIV9nz?amp=1]Discord[/url] if you have any questions!

Unspottable Demo will be playable during the Steam Game Festival (16-22 June).

Unspottable is a competitive couch party game where you need to punch your friends before they punch you.
Blend in the crowd of AI characters, hunt down the other players and use the many different environment specific rules to win the game.
"Walk like a robot and punch like a human!"

[h1]Demo Levels[/h1]

The demo will include 4 levels:

[h2]Meadow[/h2]
[u]Key elements[/u]:
[list]
[*]best level to start and to understand the core mechanics of the game.
[*]The round ends when one player has been punched.

[*]You can step on one of the floor buttons to turn off the lights for a few seconds, so you have time to hide in the dark.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36777231/0c91b4f4a0b72c67b290e705de2e2e365bb28392.jpg[/img]

notes.title: Unspottable challenges you to be a convincing NPC
notes.notes:
The RPS VidBuds have put up a bunch of let’s plays as part of Rezzed Digital, as this year’s iteration of the usual Indies Uncovered stream, and they’ve already found some solid games in the pack. But one of the surprise standouts from the bunch, for me at least, is Unspottable.

I hadn’t heard of Unspottable before, but after watching VidBud Matthew and Hardware Queen Katharine play together, I am both impressed and intrigued. It’s a multiplayer versus game where you have to blend in with a group of identical NPC robots (or robits, as is more correct), whilst also trying to spot which robits are your fellow players. Once you think you have spotted an interloper, you must deal with them in the traditional manner of dealing with interlopers: that is to say, you punch them a good’un.

notes.title: Prototyping an Unspottable level
notes.notes:
Working on Unspottable, we're trying to build new levels using the same core gameplay mechanic so the players are not lost with every new level, but adding a new twist in the gameplay so it's feels new and new strategies can be created with every level.

To do that we usually brainstorm to get a bunch of ideas, any ideas, there always a lot of bad ones but some feel good enough to make to the next stage: Prototyping.

This post shows the evolution of one of the Unspottable levels.

[b]1. We come up with the idea:
[/b]	"It would be cool to have a level where it's a bit dark and some lights the characters, so players have to avoid them!"

[b]2. Prototype the gameplay mechanic specific to that idea:
[/b][previewyoutube=tSO3jlD2s_c;full][/previewyoutube]

[b]3. We then play the prototype, and tweak it to make sure it's fun and there isn't any loophole in the gameplay.
[/b]In that case:
	- working on the number of spotlights
	- the speed of spotlights and path patterns, to avoid players staying too much in the corner or making it too easy for them to avoid them.
[previewyoutube=I9dBGsyCrFU;full][/previewyoutube]

	- Addition of an extra hiding mechanic to let people hide again after they throw a punch, in that level, turning all the lights off for a few second so it gets too dark to keep an eye on characters.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36777231/62b707fe27a9e4b5966ac0741aede24214943f9b.png[/img]

[b]4. After initial playtests with other people, if we decide the level is fun enough, we move on the art part of the level.
[/b][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36777231/0e4161d45ca9e74a9a6cdc34998b2fdfc0283cdc.png[/img]

[b]5. We make sure we make a silly gif based on the level to relax.
[/b]https://twitter.com/UnspottableGame/status/1241380022121836550

[b]6. We've got a new playable level!
[/b][previewyoutube=oLLcItpCrsU;full][/previewyoutube]


It's our first game so some of this is probably not the best example but that's pretty much how we do it, please comment if you have any advice!

notes.title: Unspottable: Blending ragdoll physics and animations
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36777231/fcd64f02cd6e73c1c298357c96824f3568d19dc7.png[/img][h2]Blending Ragdoll physics and animation in Unity
[/h2]

This is a short techincal explanation of our system to blend between ragdoll physics and animation in unity 2019.
It came from the need of adding more robots to the scene by dropping them from the sky, so after being ragdolled on the floor they had to get back to an animated state:

[previewyoutube=M8ZjZjjrxTg;full][/previewyoutube]

The ragdoll of the robots is fairly standard, they have an almost humanoid skeleton but not exactly.
It can be achieved on humanoid models following this great Brackeys video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DInV-jHm9rk

Once ragdolled on the floor, the first step is to figure out if the robot fell on its front or back.
To do that we just compare the vector up of the root bone of our character and the default vector up.
[code]Vector3.Dot(rootBone.up, Vector3.up) > 0[/code]
We're only focusing on two cases, up or down but that could be improve to have better animations to get up at different angles.

We can then choose between the two animations:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36777231/8efd2af04fd5aba6af10b4afb62882c14a806fb0.gif[/img] 
  [img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36777231/68287bb344e2436c403b57002513272b22e5ff25.gif[/img]

At that point, we want to blend between the positions of the ragdolled skeleton and the animation.
That's done by calculating the position and rotation of each bone, using their current ragdolled position and their supposed animation position.

So on [i]LateUpdate()[/i] after the animation position is calculated:
To get the animated bone position, we have to look at the transform on [i]LateUpdate[/i], but for a real humanoid rig, it should be accessible using [i]Animator.GetBoneTransform[/i] (https://docs.unity3d.com/ScriptReference/Animator.GetBoneTransform.html) 

Interpolation of position and rotation for each bone, using a blendSpeed variable to be able to tweak the strenght of the blend:
[code]foreach (Bones b in skeleton)
    {        
        b.transform.position = Vector3.Lerp(b.transform.position, b.ragdolledBonePosition, blendSpeed);
        b.transform.rotation = Quaternion.Slerp(b.transform.rotation, b.ragdolledBonePosition, blendSpeed);
    }
[/code]
I hope that short explanation helps some of you understand the logic, feel free to come and chat on twitter if you have questions!

notes.title: Presenting Unspottable
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36777231/25ba6627c2633dee431c994f96b7fe5ab6e789e3.png[/img]

GrosChevaux is a new indie game studio created by three long time friends.We've always dreamt of building games together and worked on many prototypes.

The idea for Unspottable came from a game of One Piece Unlimited Adventure on Wii. After what seemed like a bug to us in the 1v1 mode, we ended up fighting in a crowd of the same 10 characters, not knowing which one we were controlling.

We really enjoyed the experience of fighting without any indications on which character we were, nor on who our opponents were. We kept that idea in the back of our minds for 10 years!

We love some games using this hide'n'seek concept: Garry's mod Guess Who, SpyParty, Hidden in plain sight, Assassin's Creed Multiplayer mode. But we always wished more of this game were local multiplayer as that's our favorite type of gaming session!

We built on this basic concept of punching the other layers while hiding amongst AIs and create a lot of level prototypes with different rules and AIs to keep the gameplay accessible for everyone, interesting and competitive!

[previewyoutube=-utOxuGtLXA;full][/previewyoutube]

[h3]What's next?[/h3]
We currently have a playable version with 4 levels and a few more in prototype that we are currently using in playtests.

Our goal is to have 15 levels at launch and then keep prototyping and coming up with fun new concepts after that! We're hoping to release by the end of the summer 2020.

In the meantime, drop us a line, we're doing some playtests in London and Paris.

You can also find us at EGX Rezzed 2020 on Thu 26 Mar – Sat 28 Mar!

And you can get all the updates here or on twitter: [url=https://twitter.com/UnspottableGame]Twitter.com[/url]
